title: Password tutorial: raw module and curried instances
security_scope: The raw tutorial module receives PASSWORD_HASH, password and conditions through the first three pair projections, then ignores any remaining tail. It returns the exact conditions tree only when SHA256(password atom bytes) equals the expected hash atom bytes. An uncurried attacker can choose both hash and password. Separate standard-curried instances fix one public fixture hash; the intentionally insecure password design permits unsigned retargeting after disclosure. Arbitrary conditions are data at module execution, not automatically valid ledger conditions. Finite comparisons and ledger observations do not establish security or compiler preservation.

license.scope: Exact repository license retained; no independent per-file legal review.

source_span.extraction: Exact inclusive tutorial lines including comments and LF; this span is already a complete module.

source_adaptation.description: Extract the complete original module verbatim. No wrapper or narrower argument validation is added.

limitations: No upstream compiled password-module artifact is supplied by the tutorial; any measured compiler hash is a local independent reproduction, not a published .hex identity.
Raw template evidence is not password authorization: its caller supplies the expected hash. Only separately recorded instances commit to a fixed hash.
Passwords and conditions are arbitrary attacker-controlled trees; passwords and expected hashes must be atoms but are not normalized as integers or Unicode.
The tutorial explicitly warns against production use. Revealing the password permits unsigned retargeting and reuse attacks; curry does not repair this design.
VM resource observations are distinct from semantic rejection. The consensus GeneratorRuntimeError umbrella is not a closed typed semantic-rejection claim.
